The Write tool is disabled here, so the review is delivered in this message only.

## Verdict

The milestone-1 fixes match their contracts. The read-phasing integration is safe by default only because it is switched off: its acceptance rule accepts a haplotype supported by a single read, and every cached "gain" as well as the false dupC comes from exactly that. Two evaluator contracts still leak credit, and the strict projection deflates supported sensitivity for a documented but unhandled reason.

Prior fixes, checked against code and tests:

- **Alias mismatch.** Fixed as specified in `evaluation/artifacts.py:166-180`, with negative cases covered.
- **Stale running status.** Fixed with the right precedence (external failure, then running, then summary) in `artifacts.py:125-148`.
- **Flank-only phase credit.** Fixed for sample-level exactness and TN only; per-allele credit still double counts (F4).
- **Projection diagnostics.** Present and tested.
- **Specificity denominator.** Fixed in `scoring.py:273-284`, but the on-disk HiFi development evaluation was scored by the pre-fix code: it has no unresolved-negative field and reports normal specificity 5/5 while one row has `normal_false_positive: true`. No specificity number should be quoted until re-scored.
- **bcftools equivalence.** Accepted as reported; not re-run; covers only `0/1` single-ALT indels.

## Findings

**F1 HIGH. Phase acceptance has no per-haplotype read-support check.** The read list parser at `read_phasing.py:77-89` validates names and discards the haplotype column; acceptance at lines 171-183 depends only on `phase_evidence`, and `calling.py:270-277` then grants independent haplotype evidence. The WhatsHap read lists under `production_cached/current_read_phased/*/merged/read_phasing/attempt_*/assigned_reads.tsv` show the haplotype split for the four phased samples:

| Sample | Records per haplotype | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| dupc seed1701 | 12 : 1 | exact majority, chimeric minority with dupC (the FP) |
| normal seed1703 | 11 : 1 | exact majority, chimeric minority |
| normal seed1701 | 10 : 1 | exact majority, chimeric minority |
| heldout 60/62 | 6 : 9 (15 of 180 selected) | no exact gain |

The phased het sites carry AD such as 2,11 and 1,11 at QUAL 5.7 to 22.9. In every gained sample the exact sequence is the majority genotype haplotype; the minority candidate is the 60-repeat backbone plus one read's alleles, matched to the 80-repeat truth with count error -20. Any collapsed cluster with one contaminating, partial or error-prone read reproduces this. The same defect exists on the default path: `phasing.py:39-40` emits two haplotypes from a single heterozygous site with no support check. On this panel all eight development single-het records are non-same-length alleles, so it did not fire, but nothing prevents it. An undocumented experiment already exists: `production_cached/support_gate.py` and `support_gate/cached_threshold2.json` show a two-read minimum keeps 4/10 exact with zero false events and 4 missing alleles, while `support_gate/synthetic_report.json` has 57 rows losing a true haplotype at one or two minority reads. Validation needed: an integration fixture with 10:1 support and AD-consistent het calls asserting non-promotion plus recorded per-haplotype counts, then a rerun of the five cached cases. Remedy that preserves accounting: record per-haplotype selected-read counts, require a documented minimum, and when unmet emit the majority candidate with a distinct phase status and keep the second allele as a declared alias carrying the minority record count and allele list. That yields a missing allele and an unsupported candidate instead of a chimeric independent haplotype. Do not drop the minority evidence.

**F2 HIGH (upstream, documented, accounting gap). The sub-threshold length group is invisible.** `alleles.py:216-219` filters contigs below coverage before clustering and records nothing about dropped primary records. The planning note says seed1701 has 14 short, 5 long and 1 partial spans, yet `alleles.json` shows 13 primaries in contigs 49-53 with `contig_51` chosen on secondary-alignment scores and zero primaries. Same-length disambiguation and phasing therefore run on a premise the pipeline could have known was false. I could not run samtools to confirm the counts. Add sub-threshold group counts to `alleles.json`, gate phase promotion on them, and test with the seed1701 counts.

**F3 MEDIUM. One heterozygous indel under haplotype "I" voids projection for the whole allele while the consensus still asserts the ALT.** `variant_support.py:44-51, 68-70` returns `ambiguous_genotype_selection` for the entire replay. In `development/hifi/sample_dupc_40_50/summary.json` the true dupC at repeat 15, called `0/1` and applied as ALT by bcftools 1.17, now has `vcf_support: false`, status `projection_unavailable`, qual 0. HiFi development supported recall is 19/28 against 24/28 unsupported, and 29 of 57 mutation records across 16 summaries are `projection_unavailable` with no reason field because those runs predate the diagnostics. This is deflation plus an inconsistency, not a false positive. Remedy: per-record selection under "I" by replaying both alleles against the consensus, tag events explained by the het record with an explicit unphased-applied status, and keep exact support for events explained by `1/1` records. Validate with a real-bcftools test combining a `1/1` dupC and a `0/1` flank indel, then regenerate the reason histogram.

**F4 MEDIUM. Evaluator double counts identical candidates from one observation group.** Independence in `scoring.py:48-63` gates only sample-level exactness, TN and resolved call rate; lines 84-95 and 123-124 still count each prediction. A same-length cluster with a flank-only het scores 2/2 exact on a homozygous truth where the alias path scores 1/2, and a collapsed 60/80 cluster reports zero missing alleles where the alias path reports one. Add a failing test with two identical predictions, independence false, same observation group, expecting one exact, one missing, and a duplicate warning.

**F5 MEDIUM. Evaluator status derivation is fail-open.** `artifacts.py:190-207` uses deny-lists; any unknown phase or reconstruction status becomes `completed` and TN-eligible. Any new status introduced for F1 would be silently promoted. Switch to an allow-list and add a parametrized unknown-status test expecting ambiguity.

**F6 MEDIUM (reporting). The headline gains are attributable to the single-read split.** The planning note's "exact 1/10 to 4/10" and "missing 5 to 1" reflect majority haplotypes losing IUPAC bases plus three chimeras counted present by cardinality. The note shows the -20 count errors but does not attribute the table. Add an evaluator count for matched alleles with count error beyond two so chimeras are visible, and state the attribution.

**F7 LOW/MEDIUM.** `calling.py:279-280` sets `not_separately_resolved` without `candidate_duplicate_of`, relying on allele detection. Legacy `alleles.json` through the `call` or `consensus` subcommands becomes `invalid_artifacts`, which is exactly the `old_saved` seed1702 case. Add a unit test for haplotypes `["I"]` without the pointer.

**F8 LOW.** Test fixtures cannot expose the observed failure: unit read lists are 1:1, integration fixtures are 10:10, and downsampling metadata is untested.

**F9 LOW.** `docs/development.md:236` still says read-backed phase is not implemented, contradicting the limitations page and changelog. The `--min-dp` option is a documented no-op in `vcf.py:31-34` but the CLI help does not say so; AD 1,11 sites at QUAL 5.7 pass with no per-allele depth criterion, feeding F1.

**F10 LOW.** Random `attempt_*` absolute paths land in `alleles.json`, consensus context and sequence sources; reproducibility noise only.

## Reviewed files and open questions

Source: read_phasing, phasing, calling, variant_support, classify, classification_summary, consensus, vcf, alleles, tools, run_status, read_evidence, benchmarking, repeat_alignment, cli, the evaluation package, and the report template by grep. Tests: unit read_phasing, phasing, calling, variant_support, consensus, evaluation scoring, artifacts, cli, run_status; integration read_phasing, phase_consensus, variant_concordance. Docs and planning: limitations, development evaluation section, changelog by grep, dispositions, both milestone-1 notes, the three read-phasing notes, the validation report, and the tracked patch hunks for the benchmark script and allele detection. Artifacts: the cached run, debug and support-gate scripts, provenance, four read lists, three candidate VCFs, the seed1701 alleles and summary, support-gate JSONs, development HiFi evaluation totals, and the development dupc_40_50 summary.

Unresolved:

1. The `extra_event_debug` directory named in the request does not exist at the stated path or under `production_cached`, so the six-ablation claim and the source identity of the single minority read cannot be verified from artifacts.
2. The 14/5/1 span-group counts for seed1701 come from planning text, not from an independent samtools check.
3. Whether the minority read is the partial-anchor read or a long-allele read is undetermined; it changes the remedy wording, not F1.
4. All on-disk development evaluations predate the specificity and diagnostics fixes and must be regenerated before any accuracy statement.
